---
title: "What is the minimum trimmed sink rate with a 300 mm flat plate wing?"
---

{{< include _model.qmd >}}

```{python}
ENTRY_CEILING = 120.0   # s for this render, granted by the user
SOLVE_BUDGET = 15.0     # s for any one solve
PROBE_POOL = 250.0        # s granted for the probe
PROBE_SPENT = 192.8      # s the probe actually used

stall_angle = 5.75  # from 2026-09-29-05-is-naca-0006-a-valid-flat-plate-proxy-at-the-stall-bounded-reynolds-nu.qmd
span_user = 0.300
launch_height = 1.5

sink_rate, opt_plane = optimize_geometry_for_sink_rate(
    get_airplane_plate,
    alpha_max=stall_angle,
    span_max=span_user
)

v_trim = opt_plane.v_trim
flight_time = launch_height / sink_rate
root_chord = opt_plane.root_chord
tip_chord = opt_plane.tip_chord

assert flight_time < 2.0
```

::: {.hero}
[`{python} f"{sink_rate:.2f} m/s"`]{.hero-value}
[minimum trimmed sink rate]{.hero-label}
:::

**Answer.** With wing span held to [`{python} f"{span_user*1000:.0f} mm"`]{.key} and sections modelled as flat plates bounded at the [`{python} f"{stall_angle:.2f}°"`]{.key} stall limit identified in [earlier analysis](2026-09-29-05-is-naca-0006-a-valid-flat-plate-proxy-at-the-stall-bounded-reynolds-nu.qmd), the minimum trimmed sink rate degrades to [`{python} f"{sink_rate:.2f} m/s"`]{.key} at [`{python} f"{v_trim:.2f} m/s"`]{.key}. A `{python} f"{launch_height:.1f}"` m throw yields only [`{python} f"{flight_time:.2f} s"`]{.key} of flight time, so the aircraft does not meet the target (@fig-three-view-300mm). Chords expand to the [`{python} f"{root_chord*1000:.0f} mm"`]{.key} bound to recover wing area.

::: {.callout-note}
## New assumptions
1. **wing section: flat plate**, replaces NACA0006 proxy.
:::
